sections.value:
PASS WITH NOTES -- #253 round 2 at d992f6747b492e6dd80237d38ecc236d4cdca981

Reviewed only the repair delta from ac8a00daf5c0ca017d4fc858e4a0eee5ae72e913. R253-001 and R253-002 are closed for the original lost-handoff scenarios. No remaining blocker from round 1; the new notes below are C34 follow-ups, not another review round.

R253-001 CLOSED. SpawnWaits records bound independently of unanswered. Both bound() and not_answered() remove and hand off the entry when they observe the second fact, outside the mutex. This covers bind-then-drop, bind-before-stale-timeout-settlement and failure-then-bind. report_spawn_failure now retains the guard across the awaited failure construction and only settles it afterward (http/mod.rs:1903-1919). The missing route-level interrupted-build fixture is not a gate under C34: the unit bind-then-drop regression and the changed guard lifetime directly cover the relevant mechanism.

R253-002 CLOSED. Boot checks launched/answered/reported records for the current spawn_id and recovers bound as well as unbound rows. Already-bound launches hand off immediately; unbound launches hand off on registration. An answered launch and a pre-F211 historical row are ignored. The new HTTP recovery test also checks that a second completed boot does not report again.

Success-path inventory:

- --no-wait builds its response, then calls answered("dispatched"), http/mod.rs:1719-1722.
- Normal bound success builds its response, then calls answered("bound"), http/mod.rs:1759-1765.
- Bound failure/model mismatch builds the failure or named fallback, then calls answered("failed-bound"), http/mod.rs:1903-1919.
- Revive uses this same launch_seat_locked path: ordinary revive dispatches; --cheap waits for binding. There is no separate unmarked successful launch return.
- The two pre-row rollback paths call withdrawn(), not answered(). They leave no new live launch row to recover; a failed revive retains the prior row with its prior spawn_id. Pre-launch refusals have no launch receipt to settle.

Retry/withheld behavior: send failures return without spawn.reported, so an eligible launch gets at most one new reporting attempt per boot, not a timer or in-process retry loop. A committed spawn.reported suppresses later boots. Missing parent, tombstoned parent and lookup failure are explicitly distinguished but are all final withheld records; parent-lookup failure is not in the retry-on-next-boot category. There is no prime fallback, as the PR now states.

C34 follow-up -- settlement crash window. spawn_waits.rs:203-215 detaches answered/report tasks without retaining their JoinHandles. The answer can return before spawn.answered commits. Similarly, report():338-356 admits a send with a newly generated message ID before appending spawn.reported. A daemon exit between those facts can produce a false "unanswered" notice or a duplicate admitted notice on recovery. Therefore "exactly once" is proven for the in-memory handoff and completed receipts, not an atomic end-to-end guarantee across every interruption. A stable per-spawn notice ID plus tracked/drained settlement work would narrow this without a new retry loop; park_notice.rs already demonstrates stable notice IDs and admission reconciliation. Treat this as a named residual/follow-up, not a claim that the original unreported-seat recovery is still absent.

C34 follow-up -- boot cost is history-sensitive. Success adds TWO spine appends, launched and answered, not three. A failed launch additionally writes spawn.failed and, when reported, spawn.reported. No new process-launch site, timer or periodic loop is added. Recovery lists the registry once (including retired rows before its filter), then performs one indexed all_matching query per live spawned row. That query reads all three matching kinds across the seat's history, then filters the current spawn_id in memory; total work is O(registry rows + matching spawn history), not bounded solely by the live-seat count. This is once per boot, with no demonstrated cost breach, so it is a follow-up rather than a new gate. No live before/after cost measurement was run by this reviewer.

Security/correlation notes closed: the shared close-command helper applies shell_word separately to seat and pane, with a hostile-value regression. bound() requires the exact recorded seat and pane as well as spawn_id, and the negative correlation test passes. Detached reporting captures the launch rather than the registering seat's claimed parent and holds no mutex across IO. At boot, Launch::of reconstructs launch metadata from the current registry row; the spine receipts are used to identify settlement for its spawn_id. No new same-user authentication requirement is imposed.

Evidence:

- just pr-freeze 253: FINAL at the full head above, clean detached worktree, all five latest checks pass; rechecked before this verdict.
- CI run 44457191062, attempt 2: exact head; rust-test, rust-lint, check (22), check (24) all succeeded. The separate latest delivers check succeeded.
- Successful rust-test job 135336560805 identifies artifact 14498074181 in its own upload log. Its junit.xml contains 2,540 executed cases, zero failures. All seven SpawnWaits tests, both restart HTTP regressions, timeout/adapter regressions, normal bound success, model mismatch and both affected revive integration tests passed.
- Attempt 1's only failure was the unchanged real-tmux control-mode test a_lost_control_client_falls_back_then_reconnects: its tmux test server was absent. The successful attempt includes that test.
- No local build, test, mutation run, live spawn, daemon bounce or harness checks was run, per the CI-only review packet. Source worktree remains clean.
- Harness observation MW-001 records the settlement crash-window sensor as the highest-value follow-up. No additional fixture or mutation run is required to accept this final-round repair.
